rationale: C19 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both letters announce with regret that an anticipated personal appearance has become impossible, explain that circumstances require the President to remain in Washington, and ask the recipient to convey his regrets to the affected attendees. This parallel rhetorical and functional sequence is materially closer than the generic inability-to-attend language in C02 or the illness-based absence in C10.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I SEND YOU this message with exceeding regret. I was looking forward with anticipation and pleasure to revisiting Texas
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It had been my earnest hope to appear at this historic Conference
shared_material.explanation: Both open the substantive message by emphasizing the President's prior anticipation of appearing personally.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The turn of events yesterday leaves me no option--in the interest of working for peace--but to remain at the White House Wednesday
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the special circumstances of my present life...oblige me to deny myself the honor and privilege of accepting your great courtesy. It will be necessary for me to be present in Washington on Friday of this week.
shared_material.explanation: Both use an unavoidable-circumstances formulation followed by the concrete necessity of remaining in Washington on a specified day.

shared_material.child_excerpt: To all concerned-and especially to the citizens of Texas--please extend my deepest regrets
shared_material.parent_excerpt: May I hope, Mr. President, that you will express my sincere regrets to the assembled Delegates
shared_material.explanation: Both close the cancellation by directing the recipient to convey the President's regrets to the assembled or affected audience.
